# How to Turn AI Agents Into Helpful Coworkers at Work

You’ve probably heard the phrase “AI agents” tossed around at work lately. Maybe it sounded like tech jargon or something only developers need to worry about. But what if I told you these AI helpers can actually do real work for you—like sorting emails, drafting replies, or even keeping track of project updates—without you lifting a finger?

Think of an AI agent as a quiet coworker who sits inside your apps (like email, Slack, or project tools) and quietly gets things done. They don’t need coffee breaks or annual leave. They just follow instructions and help you stay focused on the work that really matters.

Here’s how you can start using them today.

---

## Start small: pick one routine task

You don’t need to automate everything at once. Start with a task that feels like a daily chore.

- **Sorting emails**: Set up a rule that tells your AI agent to flag important messages, move newsletters to a folder, and highlight anything urgent.
- **Drafting quick replies**: Use an AI agent to suggest responses to common client questions—then you just review and send.
- **Updating spreadsheets**: Give your agent access to your data and ask it to clean up duplicates, fill in missing values, or generate summaries.

*Tip: Use tools like **Claude Code** or **GitHub Copilot** if you’re comfortable with code. For non-technical users, **Microsoft Copilot** or **Google’s AI agents in Workspace** are great starting points.*

---

## Give clear instructions (and check the results)

AI agents work best when you tell them exactly what you want. Instead of vague requests like “Help me with this,” try being specific:

> “Read my inbox, flag emails from the marketing team with ‘Urgent’ in the subject, and move the rest to the ‘Newsletters’ folder.”

Or:

> “Summarise the key points from the client update in Slack channel #project-alpha and post it in #team-updates.”

The more precise your instructions, the better the agent performs. And always double-check the first few results to make sure the agent is on the right track.

---

## Use agents that connect to your tools

The best AI agents don’t live in isolation—they connect to the apps you already use.

- **Microsoft 365 Copilot**: Works inside Outlook, Teams, and Excel to help draft emails, analyse data, and generate reports.
- **Google’s AI in Workspace**: Can summarise long email threads, create action items from meeting notes, and even draft documents.
- **Slack AI**: Lets you ask questions about past conversations and get instant summaries.

These tools are designed to feel like part of your workflow, not an extra step.

---

## What this means for you

- **If you're a manager or team leader**: Use AI agents to automate routine updates. For example, set one up to generate weekly project summaries from your team’s Slack or email threads. Share these with stakeholders so everyone stays informed without extra meetings.
- **If you're in customer support**: Let an AI agent draft initial responses to common queries. You can review and personalise them before sending—saving hours each week.
- **If you're just getting started**: Pick one tool you use daily (like Gmail or Excel) and try automating a single task. Start with something simple, like sorting emails or cleaning up data. Once you see how much time it saves, you’ll want to do more.

---

## Wrap-up

AI agents aren’t here to replace you—they’re here to handle the repetitive stuff so you can focus on the work that needs your expertise. Start small, give clear instructions, and use tools that fit into your daily routine. Before you know it, you’ll have a quiet coworker doing the heavy lifting while you get on with what really matters.
